items.title: Amazon EC2 C8gn instances are now available in AWS Europe (Paris) region
items.content_snippet: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) C8gn instances, powered by the latest-generation AWS Graviton4 processors, are available in the AWS Europe (Paris) region. The C8gn instances provide up to 30% better compute performance than Graviton3-based Amazon EC2 C7gn instances. items.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory now supports fine-grained access control
items.content_snippet: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory now supports fine-grained access control (FGAC), enabling you to enforce per-user and per-tenant memory isolation through AgentCore Gateway without building custom authorization logic. With FGAC, you can front your Memory resource with an AgentCore Gateway configured for OAuth (JWT) authentication and attach Cedar policies that restrict access based on the authenticated caller's identity. items.title: Tennis (:30)
items.content_snippet: Turn your image into any art style you can imagine with ChatGPT Images.

items.title: Use Your Computer and Browser
items.content_snippet: See how ChatGPT Work can help with tasks in your desktop apps and browser. Use Computer to start music in Spotify, then combine Chrome and Google Calendar to prepare a time-off request and an out-of-office event. Learn how to share screen context with Appshots, grant access, and review the drafts before submitting or saving anything. This walkthrough uses the ChatGPT desktop app. Follow the lesson and try it yourself: https://learn.chatgpt.com/training/walkthroughs/using-your-computer-and-browse

items.title: Talk to ChatGPT Work
items.content_snippet: Brainstorm out loud and turn your ideas into a presentation with Voice in ChatGPT Work. In the desktop app, talk through ideas for a team event, ask ChatGPT to build a visual pitch deck, and review the result. You’ll also see how to continue the same task from your phone by connecting to your computer through Remote. Follow the lesson and try it yourself: https://learn.chatgpt.com/training/walkthroughs/using-voice

items.title: Create Slides, Docs, and Templates
items.content_snippet: Turn a meeting transcript into a structured Google Doc and a leadership deck with ChatGPT Work. Connect Google Drive, ask for the sections you need, and check the document against the original transcript. Then create a Google Slides presentation from the document and save both formats with Template Creator so you can use them again. Follow the lesson and try it yourself: https://learn.chatgpt.com/training/walkthroughs/creating-slides-and-docs

items.title: Use ChatGPT Work on Your Phone
items.content_snippet: Use ChatGPT Work on your phone to catch up on work and handle personal tasks before you reach your desk. Follow a Slack and Gmail catch-up, then review recent spending with the read-only Finances plugin. You’ll also see how to pair your phone with Remote to check progress and guide tasks running on your computer. For Remote, your computer needs to stay awake and online. Follow the lesson and try it yourself: https://learn.chatgpt.com/training/walkthroughs/working-on-your-phone

items.title: Build a Shareable Site
items.content_snippet: Turn a conversation into a website people can use with ChatGPT Work. Build a group-trip site with an itinerary, activity voting, and shared expenses, then refine it by asking for changes. See how to choose who can visit, manage your projects in Sites, and bring launch metrics and team updates together in a dashboard. Follow the lesson and try it yourself: https://learn.chatgpt.com/training/walkthroughs/building-a-shareable-site

items.title: Plugins & Skills
items.content_snippet: Learn how plugins and skills work together in ChatGPT Work. Use Gmail and Google Calendar to find a client’s email, schedule a kickoff, and prepare a meeting brief with links to the original sources. Then save the process as a Meeting Prep skill so you can reuse the same instructions and format for your next meeting. Follow the lesson and try it yourself: https://learn.chatgpt.com/training/walkthroughs/plugins-and-skills

items.title: Scheduled Tasks
items.content_snippet: Put a repeatable task on a schedule with ChatGPT Work. See how to use Gmail and Google Calendar to prepare meeting briefs, check the results, and schedule the task to run every weekday. Learn how to review results, change or pause tasks in the Scheduled tab, and use a saved skill to keep the format consistent. Follow the lesson and try it yourself: https://learn.chatgpt.com/training/walkthroughs/scheduled-tasks

items.title: Getting Started with ChatGPT Work
items.content_snippet: See how ChatGPT Work brings together information from your apps to help you finish a task. Set up the desktop app, choose Work, and connect Gmail and Slack. Then follow a team-dinner example: find the restaurant’s email, check the latest headcount and dietary needs, and review a reply before sending it. Follow the lesson and try it yourself: https://learn.chatgpt.com/training/walkthroughs/getting-started?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video&utm_campaign=chatgptwork_training

items.title: Which AI startups actually land enterprise contracts? — Brian Lewis, Millennium
items.content_snippet: For a given internal pain point, Brian Lewis might find 10 to 15 startups worth a look, book two or three demos, run zero or one pilot, and sign roughly one contract for every four pilots. That works out to about 5% of demo calls ending in a signature, which turns out to match published benchmarks. He is on the buying side at a hedge fund, speaking personally rather than for his employer, and the talk is a catalogue of exactly where the other 95% dies. The examples are specific enough to sting.
